rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately compare 2015 and 2016 inspection volume across total activity, routine canvass work, complaint-based work, and reinspections?
criterion: It states that completed inspection records increase from about 20,911 in 2015 to about 22,818 in 2016.
It states that routine Canvass inspections increase from 11,506 in 2015 to 12,933 in 2016.
It states that complaint-based work totals about 2,620 records in 2015 and 2,597 in 2016.
It states that reinspections increase from 3,825 in 2015 to 4,638 in 2016.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately describe the risk-category mix in the inspection extracts?
criterion: It states that high-risk establishments account for about 72.7% of 2015 inspection records and 75.1% of 2016 records.
It states that medium-risk establishments account for about 19.9% of 2015 inspection records and 19.6% of 2016 records.
It states that low-risk establishments account for about 7.3% of 2015 inspection records and 5.3% of 2016 records.
It interprets the workload as heavily concentrated in high-risk establishments.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately summarize the most important inspection outcome patterns across 2015 and 2016?
criterion: It identifies Pass as the most common result in both years.
It states that Fail outcomes increase from 3,607 in 2015 to 4,298 in 2016.
It states that Pass w/ Conditions outcomes increase from 2,158 in 2015 to 2,634 in 2016.
It states that Out of Business outcomes decline from 1,879 in 2015 to 1,546 in 2016.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo use inspection-type outcomes to draw a sound operational conclusion about problem identification versus follow-up resolution?
criterion: It notes that Complaint inspections have high fail rates in both years at roughly 31.9% in 2015 and 32.6% in 2016.
It notes that Suspected Food Poisoning inspections have especially high fail rates at roughly 39% in both years.
It notes that reinspections are mostly Pass outcomes, with 3,264 of 3,825 reinspections passing in 2015 and 3,915 of 4,638 passing in 2016.
It interprets these patterns as evidence that complaint-based work is effective at surfacing problems while many follow-up cases are resolved by reinspection.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately state the audit’s required routine-inspection frequencies and 2015 compliance findings by risk category?
criterion: It states that high-risk establishments are supposed to be inspected twice annually.
It states that medium-risk establishments are supposed to be inspected once annually.
It states that low-risk establishments are supposed to be inspected once every two years.
It states that only 43.9% of high-risk, 80.1% of medium-risk, and 24.8% of low-risk establishments received the required inspections in the audit.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo correctly distinguish between CDPH meeting its 2015 corrective action plan and still failing the full state-required inspection schedule?
criterion: It notes that CDPH met the reduced 2015 corrective action plan described in the audit.
It also states that CDPH still fell short of the full inspection frequency required by Illinois rules.
It identifies the risk that IDPH could reject future corrective action plans or revoke Local Health Protection Grant funding.
It correctly ties the grant-risk discussion to the audit’s cited 2015 LHPG amount of about $2.5 million.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo accurately report the audit’s findings on complaint and reinspection timeliness?
criterion: It states that 97.4% of critical-violation reinspections in the audit sample were completed within 48 hours of the reinspection request.
It states that 93.9% of serious-violation reinspections in the audit sample were completed within seven days of the Correct By date.
It states that 97.8% of complaint-based inspections in the audit sample were completed within 21 days of complaint receipt.
It notes that complaints involving suspected food poisoning were prioritized for a faster response of about five days.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo explicitly discuss the most important data limitations affecting interpretation of the records?
criterion: It mentions the data dictionary warning that duplicate inspection reports may still exist in the dataset.
It notes that the extracts contain only a limited field set and omit details such as violation text and complaint intake information.
It notes that the portal-based data reflects completed inspections, which limits inference about pending workload or unassigned complaints.
It notes that low-risk inspection frequency is assessed across a two-year window, so single-year event counts do not by themselves prove compliance.

rubrics.rubric: Does the memo connect the routine-inspection gap to a concrete program-capacity problem rather than treating it as a purely compliance issue?
criterion: It states that the audit found 20,900 inspections were conducted in 2015 when about 30,026 were needed.
It states that the audit estimated CDPH needed about 94 food inspectors to meet the workload.
It states that only 38 full-time sanitarians were budgeted at the time of the audit.
It identifies the staffing shortfall of 56 sanitarians as a likely driver of the routine-inspection backlog.
